title: He had everything.
paragraphs:
He had everything.
And still ended up begging… for a drop.
Pause.
Let that disturb you.
Because Gospel of Luke 16 is not fiction to entertain—it is truth to awaken. Jesus pulls back the curtain of eternity and shows us something we would rather not see:
A man can live admired… and die unprepared.

The rich man wore purple—status, influence, visible success.
Every day felt like a celebration.
Every meal, a feast.
Every moment, comfort.
At his gate?
Lazarus.

Broken skin.
Open sores.
Empty stomach.
Dogs showing more compassion than people.
And here is the silence that screams:

The rich man never touched him.
Never fed him.
Never saw him.

Not because he couldn’t…
—but because he wouldn’t.
That is the danger.

Not loud rebellion.
Not dramatic evil.
Just a slow, quiet indifference that hardens the soul until mercy feels optional.

Then suddenly—
death interrupts the story.

No warning.
No extension.
No negotiation.

Lazarus is carried by angels to Abraham’s side.
The rich man is buried—and wakes up in torment.
And just like that…
Everything flips.

The one ignored on earth is comforted in eternity.
The one celebrated on earth is now crying out in agony.
Listen closely.

The rich man doesn’t ask for escape.
He asks for relief.
“Send Lazarus… just a drop of water.”
Even in hell, he still sees Lazarus as someone beneath him.

That’s how deep sin can go.
It doesn’t just blind you—it reshapes how you see people, even in judgment.
And Abraham answers with a reality that should shake every comfortable heart:
“Between us and you, a great chasm has been fixed.”
Fixed.

No crossing.
No second chance.
No “I’ll get serious later.”
Eternity is not adjustable.
Now feel the tension rise—

The rich man suddenly becomes an evangelist.
“Send someone to warn my family!”
He believes a miracle will wake them up.
But heaven responds with something sharper than fire:
“They have Moses and the Prophets… let them hear them.”
In other words:
God has already spoken.
And then comes the line that echoes through history:
“If they do not listen… neither will they be convinced even if someone rises from the dead.”
There it is.
The shadow of the Gospel breaking through the warning.
Because Someone did rise.
Jesus Christ.

Still—many delay.
Still—many assume there is time.
Listen to me carefully.

The rich man was not condemned for having wealth.
Scripture never teaches that wealth itself is sin.
He was condemned because his heart was untouched by God.

No repentance.
No compassion.
No evidence that he knew the Lord he claimed to honor.
Faith that never moves toward mercy is not saving faith.

Because when grace enters a heart—
it changes how you see people at your gate.

You begin to notice.
You begin to care.
You begin to act.

Not to earn salvation—
but because salvation has already begun to transform you.
And here is the Gospel turn—
We are not just observers in this story.
We are the rich man.

Blessed with time.
Access to truth.
Moments of conviction.
And yet, how often do we step over what God is pointing at?
But Jesus…
He is not like the rich man.

He didn’t step over us.
He stepped toward us.
We were Lazarus—spiritually bankrupt, wounded by sin, unable to save ourselves.
And Christ came close.

He touched the unclean.
He carried our shame.
He took the fire we deserved.
On the cross, He cried out—not for a drop of water—but under the full weight of judgment.
Why?
So that sinners like us could cross from death to life.
So that the “great chasm” would not trap us—but be bridged by His blood.
This is not just a warning.
This is mercy screaming through a story.
So here’s the question that refuses to leave:
Are you living comfortably… but spiritually asleep?
Are you hearing God’s Word… but delaying obedience?
Are you surrounded by truth… but untouched by grace?
Because one day—

The gate will close.
The roles will be revealed.
And eternity will speak without interruption.
But not today.
Today, grace is still calling.
Turn.

Not tomorrow.
Not when it’s convenient.
Now.

Turn from the illusion that success equals security.
Turn from the coldness that ignores people God places in your path.
Turn from a faith that is only words.
Turn to Jesus Christ.

The risen Savior.
The only bridge across the chasm.
The only One who can take a dead heart and make it alive again.
And when He saves you—
You won’t just look up to heaven.
You will start looking differently at the people right in front of you.
The gate will no longer be a boundary.
It will become a mission.

Because eternity is real.
Souls are real.
And the Gospel is still powerful enough to rewrite any ending.
This is your moment.
Choose Christ.
Before the story becomes yours.
